Technical Documentation

CSV Check · Technical Documentation

A zero-dependency format checker for student grade CSV files — safely read UTF-8 and validate headers.

Documentation v1.1.0Python 3.x · No third-party dependencies2026-10-28

1. Overview

CSV Check is a Python command-line tool for teaching that performs a read-only check of student grade CSV files. It does not modify the file or send data over the network.

It is designed for safe, clear, immediate feedback on common problems such as encoding, delimiters and header spelling before data is imported.

What it checks

  • Reads with utf-8-sig, including Excel CSV files with a BOM.
  • Checks for a header, empty column names and duplicate column names.
  • Checks that data rows have the same number of fields as the header.
  • Checks required columns (default: id, name, score).
  • Returns three exit codes for scripting.

What it does not do

  • Modify or repair files.
  • Validate score ranges or infer data types; values are treated as strings.
  • Read Excel .xlsx files directly; save them as CSV first.

Workflow

CSV file
→
Read UTF-8
→
Validate header
→
Check required columns
→
PASS / FAIL

Project layout

After extracting the practice package, keep check.py and csvcheck/ together:

01_写作练习/
├── check.py                 # Main entry point
├── csvcheck/
│   ├── __init__.py          # Core logic: inspect_csv()

│   ├── students.csv         # PASS

└── README.md
NoteCopying check.py without csvcheck/ causes ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'csvcheck'.

3. Quick start

In Windows CMD, change to the script directory and run the checker. Adjust the paths for your computer:

cd "C:\Users\Teacher\Downloads\发给学生_技术文档写作 (1)\学生实践包\01_写作练习"
"C:\Users\Teacher\python-sdk\python3.13.2\python.exe" check.py samples\students.csv

If Python is on your PATH, use:

python check.py samples\students.csv

4. Command-line arguments

python check.py <CSV file path> [--require COL1 COL2 ...]
ArgumentTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
filePositional stringYes—Relative or absolute path to the CSV file.
--requireOptional, space-separated valuesNoid name scoreRequired column names; case-sensitive and order-independent.

Examples

Default required columns

python check.py samples\students.csv

Custom required columns

python check.py 2026秋季成绩.csv --require 学号 姓名 成绩 班级

This checks that all four named columns appear in the header.

No required columns

python check.py data.csv --require

This checks readability and header validity without requiring specific column names.

5. Step-by-step guide

  1. Check Python. Run python --version. If the command is unavailable, install Python or use its full path.
  2. Open a terminal. On Windows 11, press Win, type cmd or PowerShell, and press Enter.
  3. Change to the script directory.
    cd "C:\Users\Teacher\Downloads\发给学生_技术文档写作 (1)\学生实践包\01_写作练习"
    TipQuote paths containing spaces. Replace the example path with your own.
  4. Run the check.
    "C:\Users\Teacher\python-sdk\python3.13.2\python.exe" check.py samples\students.csv

    In PowerShell, prefix a quoted executable path with the call operator:

    & "C:\Users\Teacher\python-sdk\python3.13.2\python.exe" check.py samples\students.csv
  5. Read the report. Check the exit code with echo %errorlevel% in CMD or $LASTEXITCODE in PowerShell.

6. Expected output

The practice package includes four sample files. The screenshots show actual runs.

✅ students.csv — PASS
All three columns are present; three data rows; exit code 0.
⚠️ missing-name.csv — FAIL
The name column is missing; exit code 1.
❌ empty.csv — ERROR
The file is empty and has no header; exit code 2.
❌ students.tsv — tab-delimited
The tab-delimited file does not have the expected comma-separated columns; exit code 1.

Report fields

FieldMeaning
CSV Check X.Y.ZTool version.
File: ...The supplied file path.
Data rows: NData rows, excluding the header and blank rows.
Columns: a, b, cColumn names read from the header.
Missing columns: nameRequired names absent from the header, or none.
Result: PASS / FAILWhether all required columns are present.

7. Exit codes

The script returns an integer through sys.exit(code), allowing batch files and CI workflows to branch on the result.

CodeStatusMeaningNext step
0PASSChecks passed.Continue processing.
1FAILRequired columns are missing.Fix the header or change --require.
2ERRORThe file cannot be read or has a serious format problem.Check encoding, delimiters and header.

Use in a script

#!/bin/bash
python check.py grades.csv
case $? in
  0) echo "Passed; import data" ;;
  1) echo "Missing columns; fix the header" ;;
  2) echo "File error; check encoding and format" ;;
esac

8. Troubleshooting

A: python is not recognized

Python may not be on PATH or Windows may be using an app store alias. Locate the executable, call it by its full path, or add its directory to your user PATH and reopen the terminal. In PowerShell you can search with:

Get-ChildItem -Path "$env:USERPROFILE" -Recurse -Filter "python.exe" -Depth 5

B: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'csvcheck'

Ensure check.py and csvcheck/ are together and change to the correct directory. Use dir to inspect it.

C: ERROR: File has no header.

The file may be empty or contain only blank lines. Make sure the first row contains column names such as id,name,score, and save as UTF-8 CSV.

D: ERROR: Cannot read a UTF-8 CSV file

Check the file encoding, comma delimiter and field counts. Convert tab-separated files to CSV, save text as UTF-8, and inspect the row named in any field-count error for missing or extra commas.

E: No output

Run python --version to verify the executable. If Windows is invoking a store alias instead, try the full path to Python.

F: PowerShell reports a syntax error for a path with spaces

Use the call operator before a quoted executable path:

& "C:\Program Files\MyPython\python.exe" check.py file.csv
Capture diagnosticsTo share both standard output and errors with a teacher or classmate:
& "full path to python.exe" check.py file.csv 2>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath debug.txt

9. Source structure

check.py — CLI entry point

Parses arguments, calls inspect_csv(), formats the report and returns an exit code. The following is a simplified sketch:

import argparse
import sys
from csvcheck import inspect_csv, CsvCheckError, __version__

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(...)
    parser.add_argument("file", ...)
    parser.add_argument("--require", ...)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    report = inspect_csv(args.file, args.require)
    return 0 if report["valid"] else 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

csvcheck/__init__.py — core logic

inspect_csv(path, required_columns) returns a dictionary:

FieldTypeDescription
columnsList[str]Header names
row_countintData rows, excluding header and blanks
missing_columnsList[str]Missing required columns
validboolWhether all required columns are present

Ideas for extension

  • Validate score ranges in inspect_csv().
  • Add a --json option using the existing format_report() in csvcheck/__main__.py.
  • Accept multiple file arguments and loop over them to check a batch.
